title: Foresight AI Brings Gremlin Agents to Reliability Engineering
source_used: InfoQ; announcement date checked on Help Net Security (7 Oct 2026)
key_facts: Gremlin, a reliability-management company, announced general availability of Foresight AI, an agentic add-on to the Gremlin platform that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to check that a fix works; Help Net Security carried the announcement on 7 Oct 2026, InfoQ on 11 Oct 2026.

The product splits work between four agent roles: an Analyst that gathers service data and recommends tests, a Tester that schedules and runs them, an Operator that interprets failed tests and proposes fixes, and a Technical Program Manager that tracks coverage and risks and can send weekly reports through Slack.

Recommendations rest on Gremlin's Failure Atlas, a proprietary record the company says is built from millions of fault-injection experiments over more than ten years across tens of thousands of distributed systems.
Gremlin says system data is not used to train a large language model; the agents use platform data and the Failure Atlas, with an LLM used for searching, summarising and explaining results.
Gremlin says Foresight AI will neither run a test nor apply a fix without approval, so an engineer stays responsible for changes.
It also builds reports and dashboards from natural-language requests, meant to show changes in reliability scores and the risks teams have addressed.

Intellyx analyst Jason English, writing for Gremlin, calls observability and AI SRE products largely reactive and cautions that a reliability programme cannot simply be installed; Intellyx discloses that Gremlin is its customer.
InfoQ notes the evidence so far comes from Gremlin and its beta programme, and the company has not published comparative accuracy data, false-positive rates or detailed beta results.
